answer: The largest gap in cancer screening participation in Finland is associated with education level in cervical cancer screening. According to preliminary 2025 data from the Finnish Cancer Registry, participation rates are 50.3% for the group with primary education or unknown education, compared to 80.8% for those with tertiary/higher education. This represents a gap of 30.5 percentage points, which is larger than the regional breast screening participation gap (9.5 percentage points) and the native-language-associated cervical screening gap (19.7 percentage points) reported in the same sources [S1, S2, S3].

# Evidence-Based Equity Gaps and Decision Support Candidates

## 1. Regional breast-screening participation gap — observed 2024

The Finnish Cancer Registry reports **81.6%** breast screening participation nationwide (excluding Åland), compared with **74.3% in the City of Helsinki**, **76.1% in West Uusimaa** and **85.6% in North Ostrobothnia**. The difference between these last two regional observations is **9.5 percentage points**.
